originator: Robert McColley (attributed by trade; no documentation)
parentage: Philodendron erubescens (unknown if hybrid cross or spontaneous mutation)
notes: ORIGIN DEBATE: No official answer. Two competing theories: (1) Intentional hybrid of P. erubescens by Robert McColley at Bamboo Nurseries, Orlando FL in the 1970s — widely repeated but NO patent, breeding record, or nursery catalog has surfaced. (2) Spontaneous mutation (sport) from tissue culture of P. erubescens — supported by unstable variegation and somaclonal variation patterns. A 2025 micropropagation study (Khumkarjorn, Thailand) confirms it is P. erubescens 'Pink Princess'. Parent of patented mutant EM0003 (PP36881).

originator: unknown (possibly related to McColley's P. erubescens line; unconfirmed)
parentage: Philodendron erubescens (unknown if hybrid or sport)
notes: ORIGIN DEBATE: No official answer. Commonly grouped with Pink Princess as products of McColley's breeding program but no patent or registration exists. Some believe it is a spontaneous tissue culture mutation. Distinguished by pink-tinged stems (vs. White Knight's burgundy stems and White Wizard's green stems).

introduced_year: early 2010s (if Costa Farms claim is accurate); unknown (trade history)
originator: CONFLICTING CLAIMS: (1) Costa Farms — developed by their horticulturists in Florida in early 2010s as P. bipinnatifidum 'White Knight' with PVP #201800127. (2) Trade history — unknown originator, climbing P. erubescens type with burgundy stems
parentage: CONFLICTING: (1) Costa Farms — P. bipinnatifidum variegated form. (2) Trade — unknown, possibly P. erubescens related
notes: ORIGIN CONTROVERSY: Two completely different plants using the same trade name. Costa Farms version is a self-heading P. bipinnatifidum type with PVP #201800127. Collector version is a climbing P. erubescens type with burgundy stems. These are morphologically DIFFERENT plants.

ORIGIN DEBATE: No official answer. PlantCircle states: 'All three plants [White Wizard, White Princess, White Knight] are hybrids with unknown parentage due to lack of documentation proving the lineage. We can only guess that some may have come from tissue culture labs in the Netherlands or Thailand.' Distinguished by completely green stems with sectoral variegation.

parentage: Sport of Philodendron 'Florida' (P. pedatum x P. squamiferum, McColley 1951)
notes: A sport of the Philodendron 'Florida' hybrid created by Robert McColley in 1951 at Bamboo Nurseries, Orlando FL. Creamy-white to mint-green new leaves that darken with age. Sometimes labeled 'Florida Ghost Mint'. Variegation is unstable.

parentage: Sport of Philodendron 'Florida' (P. pedatum x P. squamiferum, McColley 1951)
notes: Sport selection of the original Philodendron 'Florida' hybrid (McColley 1951). Irregular creamy-white variegation. Some sources note possible additional parentage beyond P. pedatum x P. squamiferum.

The original Philodendron 'Florida' created in 1951 by Robert McColley at Bamboo Nurseries, Orlando FL. 'Florida Green' is the non-variegated form. McColley also created 'Florida Compacta' using a more compact P. squamiferum crossed with P. quercifolium.

trade_name: Mamei / Silver Cloud / Quilted Silver Leaf
originator: Édouard André (discovered/collected wild specimen in Ecuador, 1882)
notes: MISLABELING CONTROVERSY: This is a wild species, not a cultivar. 'Silver Cloud' is a TRADE NAME/MISLABEL from wholesale nurseries. No ICRA cultivar registration exists. Also confused with P. pastazanum (round petioles vs. mamei's flat/ruffle petioles).
Wild species native to southeast Brazil, endangered in habitat. Sometimes confused with Epipremnum 'Silver Sword' (different plant).

originator: N/A (wild species — Philodendron hederaceum var. hederaceum)
notes: Wild species/variety (P. hederaceum var. hederaceum, formerly P. micans). Native to Mexico to Caribbean. Formerly sold under names P. cordatum, P. micans, P. miduhoi, P. oxycardium, P. scandens.

originator: Discovered by M. André of Paris; introduced by Veitch Nurseries
notes: Wild species endemic to Colombia (Chocó and Antioquia). Name means 'black gold' — golden sparkles on dark leaves.
Wild species native to Colombia. Parent of 'Philodendron Glorious' (P. gloriosum x P. melanochrysum), bred by Keith Henderson in Cairns, Australia, 1970s.

originator: N/A (wild species — described by L. Mathieu ex Schott, 1856)
notes: Wild species native to Costa Rica to Peru. Many ecotypes exist. Marketing names like 'Red Back', 'Mini', 'Dwarf Ecuador' are not registered cultivars.

originator: N/A (wild species — named after Luis Sodiro; described by N.E. Brown, 1883)
notes: Wild species native to Colombia. Once thought synonymous with P. ornatum. Silver mottling on green, cordate leaves.

trade_name: Paraiso Verde / Marina Ruy Barbosa Philodendron
originator: Linked to Mr. Natalino's nursery in Belém, Brazil; named by Chandra G. Hendarto
notes: Linked to Mr. Natalino's nursery in Belém, Brazil. Named by Chandra G. Hendarto. No specific breeder or patent identified.

originator: Roberto Burle Marx (attributed, but this is a wild species)
parentage: Wild species — Philodendron imbe or related
notes: Associated with Brazilian landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx, but this is likely a wild species popularized through his nursery. Burle Marx was a collector, not a breeder. Plant may have been named in his honor.

originator: N/A (wild species — described by K. Krause)
notes: Wild species native to southern Colombia to Bolivia. Climbing epiphyte with heavy silver variegation on juvenile leaves.

originator: N/A (wild species — described by George S. Bunting, 1987)
notes: Wild species native to Espírito Santo, Brazil. New population discovered 2024, 128 km away with ~50 individuals. More plants exist in cultivation than in the wild.

originator: N/A (wild species — described by M.L. Soares & Mayo, 2001)
notes: Wild species native to northern Brazil and Bolivia. Name 'tortum' means 'twist' — fern-like, twisted leaves.

originator: Joep Moonen (discovered); Thomas B. Croat (formally described)
parentage: Natural hybrid — Philodendron bipennifolium x P. pedatum (presumed)
notes: Naturally occurring hybrid (nothospecies). Only two wild specimens known. Cultivar name 'Joep' established in Aroideana 33:267 (2010).
Wild species native to the Guianas and northern Brazil. Sometimes confused with P. spiritus-sancti when young.

originator: N/A (wild species — described by G.S. Bunting, 1975)
notes: Wild species native to Amazonas state, Venezuela, around the Atabapo River.
Wild species from Chocó region of Colombia. Renamed Philodendron rubrijuvenilum in 2021. Juvenile leaves bright red.

originator: N/A (wild species — described by T.B. Croat & C.C. Finch, 2004)
notes: Wild species native to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and northern Brazil.

originator: unknown (trade name, not a distinct cultivar)
parentage: Trade name applied to Philodendron mamei and possibly other species

ORIGIN DEBATE: The Spruce contradicts itself — calls it both 'a naturally occurring P. erubescens hybrid' (impossible — hybrids don't occur naturally in cultivation). Likely a spontaneous mutation selected from P. erubescens stock.

parentage: Tissue-cultured cultivar of Monstera deliciosa (natural mutation)
notes: Developed ~2020 in Thailand via tissue culture. Costa Farms holds patent. Early specimens sold for up to $15,000.

parentage: Variegated sport of Monstera deliciosa var. borsigiana
notes: Variegated form with white/cream variegation. Unstable. Possibly European or Japanese origin, undocumented.
Yellow-variegated form. Less common than Albo or Thai Constellation.
Mint-green variegated form. More sectoral/splotchy than Thai Constellation.
Wild species native to southern Mexico to Panama. In cultivation since early 1800s.

trade_name: Monstera Peru / Green Galaxy / Epipremnum Marble Planet (mislabel)
notes: SPECIES vs. CULTIVAR CONTROVERSY: NOT a described species. 'Monstera karstenianum' is NOT valid — never formally described. An undescribed species from Peru. Mislabeled as Epipremnum 'Marble Planet' or 'Green Galaxy.'

trade_name: Variegated Adansonii / Variegated Swiss Cheese Plant
parentage: Variegated sport of Monstera adansonii (wild species)
notes: Variegated sport of M. adansonii. Unstable. Multiple forms (white, yellow, mint) with no documented originators.

trade_name: Marble Planet Devil's Ivy / Marble Planet Pothos
notes: New cultivar of E. pinnatum. Sometimes confused with Monstera Peru (also sold as 'Green Galaxy' or 'Epipremnum Marble Planet').
